name: es31-multisample-textures
title: Multisample textures and the sample mask
summary: glTexStorage2DMultisample (fixedsamplelocations TRUE and FALSE) rendered into through framebuffer attachments, every sample read back exactly with texelFetch of sampler2DMS / isampler2DMS / usampler2DMS (each sample given its own content with glSampleMaski), textureSize, glGetMultisamplefv, the sample-count and sample-mask limits, glGetInternalformativ on TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE, the sample mask on a triangle's partial coverage, and the INVALID_ENUM / INVALID_VALUE / INVALID_OPERATION cases of ES 3.2 sections 8.8, 8.10, 8.11, 9.2, 13.8.3 and 20.3. Nothing depends on the implementation-defined sample positions.
spec: ES 3.2 §8.8 Multisample Textures (glTexStorage2DMultisample, sample count rule, fixedsamplelocations, errors)
ES 3.2 §8.10 Texture Parameters (sampler state is INVALID_ENUM on multisample targets), §8.11.3 Texture Level Parameter Queries, §8.18 Immutable-Format Texture Images

ES 3.2 §9.2.3.1 Multisample Queries (SAMPLES, SAMPLE_BUFFERS), §9.2.8 Attaching Texture Images to a Framebuffer (TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE attachments), §9.2.4 / §9.2.6 Renderbuffer Objects and Queries (RENDERBUFFER_SAMPLES), §9.4.2 Whole Framebuffer Completeness (INCOMPLETE_MULTISAMPLE)
ES 3.2 §11.1.3.3 Multisample Texel Fetches, §11.1.3.4 Texture Queries (textureSize)
ES 3.2 §13.4 Multisampling (GetMultisamplefv, SAMPLE_POSITION), §13.8.3 Multisample Fragment Operations (SAMPLE_MASK, SampleMaski), Appendix A Invariance

ES 3.2 §20.3 Internal Format Queries (SAMPLES / NUM_SAMPLE_COUNTS on TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE), chapter 21 state tables (MAX_SAMPLE_MASK_WORDS, MAX_COLOR_TEXTURE_SAMPLES, MAX_DEPTH_TEXTURE_SAMPLES, MAX_INTEGER_SAMPLES)
GLSL ES 3.10 §8.9.1 Texture Query Functions (textureSize(gsampler2DMS)), §8.9.2 Texel Lookup Functions (texelFetch(gsampler2DMS, ivec2, int sample)), §4.7.4 Default Precision Qualifiers

api.glTexStorage2DMultisample: RGBA8 (fixedsamplelocations TRUE and FALSE), RGBA8UI, RGBA8I, RGB10_A2, RG8, R8, SRGB8_ALPHA8, DEPTH_COMPONENT16/24/32F, DEPTH24_STENCIL8, DEPTH32F_STENCIL8 allocated with every sample count glGetInternalformativ reports (SAMPLES of the attached framebuffer between the request and the next larger count; every sample of RGBA8/RGBA8UI/RGBA8I written and read back exactly); the sample count and fixedsamplelocations observed through framebuffer completeness; INVALID_ENUM for target TEXTURE_2D and for RGB9_E5, INVALID_VALUE for samples 0, width/height 0 and width > MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, INVALID_OPERATION for too many samples, texture 0 and a texture that already has storage
api.glGetMultisamplefv: SAMPLE_POSITION of every sample of fixed and non-fixed textures in [0, 1]; identical for two fixedsamplelocations textures of different size and format; INVALID_VALUE for index == SAMPLES, 1000, and on the single-sample default framebuffer
api.glSampleMaski: word 0 set to 0, all ones, 0x55555555, 0xAAAAAAAA, bits beyond SAMPLES, one bit per sample, all but one sample, 0xA5A5A5A5 (read back): the samples written are exactly the ones the mask lets through, also on a triangle's partial coverage; INVALID_VALUE for MAX_SAMPLE_MASK_WORDS
api.glEnable: SAMPLE_MASK restricts writes to the masked samples and is ignored by a single-sample framebuffer (SAMPLE_BUFFERS = 0); DEPTH_TEST for the per-sample depth writes
api.glDisable: SAMPLE_MASK disabled: a stored mask of 0 is ignored and every sample is written; DITHER disabled for exact 8-bit results
api.glIsEnabled: SAMPLE_MASK false initially, true after glEnable, false after glDisable
api.glGetIntegeri_v: SAMPLE_MASK_VALUE of every word is all ones initially and equals the value set with glSampleMaski
api.glGetIntegerv: MAX_SAMPLE_MASK_WORDS, MAX_COLOR/DEPTH_TEXTURE_SAMPLES, MAX_INTEGER_SAMPLES, MAX_SAMPLES, MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE, and SAMPLES / SAMPLE_BUFFERS of the draw framebuffer (multisample texture attached: SAMPLES = its sample count, SAMPLE_BUFFERS 1; single-sample: 0 and 0)
api.glGetInternalformativ: NUM_SAMPLE_COUNTS and SAMPLES on TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE for twelve formats: positive and descending, the largest at least the limit section 20.3.1 names; count 1 writes only the maximum, count 0 writes nothing; INVALID_VALUE for count -1, INVALID_ENUM for RGB9_E5
api.glGetTexLevelParameteriv: TEXTURE_WIDTH, TEXTURE_HEIGHT and TEXTURE_INTERNAL_FORMAT of level 0 of a multisample texture equal the allocation; level 1 and -1 -> INVALID_VALUE
api.glGetTexParameteriv: TEXTURE_IMMUTABLE_FORMAT is TRUE for a multisample texture
api.glTexParameteri: MIN_FILTER and WRAP_S on TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE -> INVALID_ENUM, BASE_LEVEL 1 -> INVALID_OPERATION, BASE_LEVEL 0 accepted
api.glTexStorage2D: target TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE -> INVALID_ENUM; single-sample RGBA8 / RGBA32I / RGBA32UI 1024 x 32 targets for the fetched samples
api.glBindTexture: a multisample texture bound to TEXTURE_2D -> INVALID_OPERATION; TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE bound to the sampler unit for every fetch
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE attached as color 0 and as depth / depth-stencil: rendering into it is read back sample by sample; level 1 -> INVALID_VALUE; TEXTURE_2D with a multisample texture and TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE with a 2D texture -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: COMPLETE for every allocated format and count; INCOMPLETE_MULTISAMPLE for a fixedsamplelocations FALSE texture with a renderbuffer, for two textures that differ in fixedsamplelocations, and for a multisample texture with a single-sample texture; COMPLETE for a texture + renderbuffer with equal sample counts and fixed locations
api.glGenFramebuffers: one framebuffer per multisample texture, three single-sample result framebuffers
api.glBindFramebuffer: multisample framebuffers as draw targets, single-sample ones as the fetch targets, the window for the final cells
api.glGenRenderbuffers: a multisample renderbuffer for the completeness rules
api.glBindRenderbuffer: target of the renderbuffer storage call
api.glRenderbufferStorageMultisample: RGBA8 renderbuffer with the texture's sample count: RENDERBUFFER_SAMPLES decides whether the mixed framebuffer is complete
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: multisample renderbuffer attached next to a multisample texture
api.glGetRenderbufferParameteriv: RENDERBUFFER_SAMPLES compared with the texture's sample count
api.glClearBufferfv: sentinel before every float fetch: a draw that wrote nothing would fail the exact comparison
api.glClearBufferiv: sentinel before every signed integer fetch and before every textureSize query
api.glClearBufferuiv: sentinel before every unsigned integer fetch
api.glClear: depth cleared to 1 in the depth samples test; window cleared to black
api.glClearDepthf: 1.0: every depth sample is overwritten by the per-sample depth draws (ALWAYS)
api.glDepthFunc: ALWAYS: each sample receives its own depth through the sample mask; read back through sampler2DMS
api.glDepthMask: TRUE during the per-sample depth writes
api.glReadPixels: RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE, RGBA_INTEGER/INT and RGBA_INTEGER/UNSIGNED_INT readback of the single-sample targets that the samples were fetched into, and of the window
api.glViewport: target-sized viewports for the pattern draws, strip-sized viewports for the fetches, 128 x 128 cells for the window
api.glUseProgram: pattern, triangle, fetch, show and size programs per sampler kind
api.glGetUniformLocation: u_ms, u_sample, u_texels, u_z, u_tri, u_size, u_origin, u_cell, u_samples, u_cols located; their effects are visible in the results
api.glUniform1i: sampler unit, pattern number, cell geometry
api.glUniform1f: NDC depth of the depth writes, target size of the triangle
api.glUniform2i: texture size and window cell origin
api.glUniform2fv: triangle corners; classified pixels match its geometry
api.glDrawArrays: one triangle per pattern draw, per fetch and per window cell

visual_review.notes: 256x256 radeonsi es-max capture viewed (llvmpipe and zink captures are byte-identical to it; all three use 4 samples). Four 128x128 cells, each a 2x2 grid of 64x64 sub-cells, one per sample, with the 16x12 texels visible as 4x5-pixel blocks. Every sub-cell is a smooth gradient (red growing to the right, green upwards) with a diagonal seam where an 8-bit channel wraps, and the seam position and the blue level change from sample to sample, so the four samples of a cell are clearly distinct. The four cells (RGBA8 fixed, RGBA8 not fixed, RGBA8UI, RGBA8I) look the same, as they should: they hold the same pattern numbers. No black sub-cells, stray pixels or seams between cells.
